newsitem.title: USA: Sun Micro hires Canepa to head server unit.
newsitem.headline: Sun Micro hires Canepa to head server unit.

text.p: In an apparent industry coup, Sun Microsystems Inc said Mark Canepa has accepted the position of vice president of Sun Microsystems Computer Co's rapidly-growing Workgroup Server Products Group.

Canepa is a 20-year veteran of Hewlett-Packard Co who had served as general manager of HP's workstation operations before being named last month to head Compaq Computer Corp's newly-formed Workstation Division.
Canepa was not immediately available for comment, but said in a statement the decision was based on the opportunity to work at Sun and on existing personal ties in the Boston area.

Sun Microsystems recently announced plans to expand business operations and invest in a new campus in the Boston, Mass., area, where it already employs more than 1,000 in its largest U.S. operations outside of Silicon Valley.
"The opportunity to work with a dynamic company such as Sun, together with our personal ties in the Boston area, made it a clear decision for my family and myself," Canepa said.

On September 25, Compaq Computer said Canepa had been named vice president of the Workstation Division it formed on August 5 as part of plans to launch a family of Microsoft Windows NT-based workstations in the fourth quarter.

A Compaq spokesman was not immediately available for comment. The company said previously that Canepa would have a hand in a unit which was a cornerstone in Compaq's strategy to become "one of the top three computer companies by the year 2000."

At Sun, Canepa will report directly to John Shoemaker, vice president and general manager of the Enterprise Server and Storage Group. Its workgroup server products compete with low-end servers for Unix and Microsoft/Intel platforms.
Canepa holds B.S. and M.S. degrees in electrical engineering from Carnegie-Mellon University and an executive M.B.A. from University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School.

A Compaq spokeswoman said later that Canepa had made the decision on his own and had spoken with John Rose, Compaq's senior vice president and group general manager of its enterprise computing group about it earlier in the day.
"He left for personal reasons," she said, noting his family's preference for residing in the Boston area.
Mike Perez, a Compaq executive, will take temporary responsibility for the workstation group, she said.
